objective: Benchmark Project SkyNet Heavy-Lifter v2 internal cost structures against global commercial drone delivery standards, incorporating regulatory and consumer constraints from internal documents.
decision_question: Should OmniLogistics adjust its fleet mix and capital allocation for Project SkyNet to comply with UAM regulations and address consumer concerns, while achieving the projected 35% cost reduction by Q4 2027?

Regulatory Compliance.Weight Limit: Heavy-Lifter v2 exceeds 25 lbs by 2.5 lbs; must prioritize Swift-Class (18 lbs) for urban corridors.
Regulatory Compliance.Altitude & Restricted Zones: Operations limited to 150-300 ft; no flights over schools, events, government buildings.

Cost Structure.Capital Expenditure: $45.5M total; $22M hardware, $12.5M software, $4.5M compliance, $3M marketing, $3.5M contingency.

Consumer Acceptance.Willingness to Pay: 55% willing to pay up to $2.50 premium for 30-min delivery.

Fleet Economics.Heavy-Lifter v2: Exceeds weight limit; limited urban use.
Fleet Economics.Swift-Class: 18 lbs; compliant; prioritize for urban centers.
Fleet Economics.Fleet Mix: Recalibrate to balance compliance and cost efficiency.

hypotheses.hypothesis: H1: Replacing Heavy-Lifter v2 with Swift-Class drones in urban corridors will increase per-package cost but ensure regulatory compliance, potentially delaying break-even.
H2: Investing in Whisper-Prop technology and camera shutters will increase consumer acceptance and willingness to pay premium, offsetting higher operational costs.
H3: The 35% cost reduction target ($2.66/package) is achievable only if Swift-Class drones achieve similar economies of scale as Heavy-Lifter v2.
H4: External benchmarks will show that OmniLogistics' cost structure is competitive but compliance costs are higher due to weight limit issues.

The demand pool for Project SkyNet Heavy-Lifter v2 Fleet Economics: Internal Cost Structures Benchmarked Against Global Commercial Drone Delivery Standards is large enough to deserve resource-allocation debate.
